Pulse for 22 October 2026

The stories from 22 October 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

Everyday tool

Claude asks you less often

Auto mode is a setting where a classifier, a check that sorts each step as safe or risky, approves Claude's routine actions so you are not asked every time.

Study

AI beats doctors in a test

The Diagnostic Orchestrator is a Microsoft system that plays the roles of several doctors around one case, and a paper in Science says it diagnosed old case files more often than the general doctors in the study.

Everyday tool

Let AI log in for you

1Password for Agents is a way for an AI agent, software that finishes tasks for you, to sign in to a site while the password stays inside the password manager.

New model

AI now chooses in a blink

The Decisions API is a service that takes a question with a fixed set of answers and returns one choice, plus how confident it is, and OpenAI has now opened it to every customer.

Everyday tool

Canva now designs posters

Canva Craft is an image model from Canva, the first the company trained itself, built to plan a designed page and then draw it, and it is available to every Canva user.

Everyday tool

AI checks code with proofs

A formal proof is a machine-checked argument that a stated rule holds for every input inside its assumptions, and Anthropic says Claude wrote such proofs for tests in 123 open-source libraries.

Everyday tool

AI draws editable logos

Ideogram Vector is an image model that returns an SVG, a file made of shapes rather than a grid of pixels, so a logo can be scaled and recolored.

Everyday tool

Every Uber employee gets AI

ChatGPT Work is an agent, a program that carries out a multi-step office task and returns a finished file, and Uber is giving it to its whole workforce of about 30,000 people.

Everyday tool

Show AI tasks by video

Record for agent is a Loom recording mode that turns a short narrated screen video into a written prompt an assistant can follow.

AI agents

AI agents research in teams

A reasoning atlas is a stack of short research reports, and OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research had thousands of AI agents write one from a mouse-brain experiment in 32 minutes.

AI agents

Banks limit AI agent access

An AI agent is a program that can carry out steps for you, and several large US banks say they are finding such agents inside customer accounts, often signed in with the customer's own password.

AI agents

One agent is often enough

A subagent is a helper with its own notebook, tools, and instructions, and Anthropic says one main agent that loads those instructions only when a task needs them often beat a crowd of helpers on quality.
